opus.why: Incident reconstruction from a short log. The hard parts are the order of cause and effect, the PAYMENT_UNKNOWN order that was never resolved, and the DB pool still running out after resume. It needs careful reasoning that sticks to the evidence, but Sonnet at high effort matches the top models here.

fable.why: Incident timeline reconstruction with a strict 'don't guess' constraint; needs to spot that db pool exhaustion recurs after recovery and order 88133 is left in PAYMENT_UNKNOWN. Sonnet reads this precisely; Haiku risks over-concluding or missing the lingering states.

opus.why: Telling firm decisions apart from floated ideas and checking each against an 8-line brief. Mild nuance (VO options, 'not in this round' for vertical), but bounded and well within Sonnet.

fable.why: Distinguishing firm decisions from floated ideas ('maybe female VO' vs 'send two options', 'not in this round' vs brief's 9:16 requirement) and cross-checking against the brief needs careful judgment; Sonnet medium is enough, Opus adds nothing.

opus.why: A short Russian chat to sort into agreed vs pending items for logo and palette. Simple extraction with a little judgment on the unresolved green; internal notes, not final copy.

fable.why: Short Russian chat; agreed items (concept 2, bolder mark, warm palette, middle orange) and open items (green, font) are explicit in the text. Haiku at high effort extracts this reliably with no quality loss.

opus.why: A three-bullet TL;DR of one paragraph. Trivial summarisation.

fable.why: Three-bullet TL;DR of a one-paragraph summary. Trivial compression task; Haiku low matches any model.

opus.why: Sorting real blockers (TTL unit bug, persisted passwordHash, Redis failure mode, KEYS blocking) from nits needs solid engineering judgment. The comment set is small and clear, so Sonnet is enough.

fable.why: Needs engineering judgment to separate real blockers (TTL unit bug, plaintext passwordHash in redis, keys('*') in prod, redis-down behavior) from nits and follow-ups. Security-flavored triage where Haiku may misclassify; Sonnet medium is sufficient.

opus.why: Cross-evaluator synthesis with contradictions, ship risks (including a legal claim) and a prioritised recommendation. It's creative and strategic judgment, though the inputs are small. Sonnet at high effort holds quality.

fable.why: Cross-source synthesis: agreements, contradictions (A vs B on the opening), risks (unsubstantiated '#1' claim), and a prioritized fix order on a brand film. Creative/brand judgment where quality shows; Sonnet high holds, Opus not needed for three short files.

opus.why: A follow-up asking to rank the audit's risks with owners and flag deadlines before month end (25 and 30 Nov, given today is 18 Nov). Short doc, moderate ranking judgment.

fable.why: Follow-up extraction: list risks, rank, attach owners, flag deadlines before Nov 30 (font licence 25 Nov, logo 30 Nov). Mostly explicit in the doc; Haiku high handles ranking and date checks without a drop.

opus.why: Turning messy Russian meeting notes into ADRs plus open questions with who argued for what. Structured extraction with some judgment on decided vs not decided. Internal doc.

fable.why: Turn messy Russian meeting notes into ADRs (context/decision/consequences) and separate undecided debates with who argued what. Requires judgment on what counts as a decision and clean structured Russian output; Sonnet medium matches top quality.

opus.why: Grouping about 20 comments into complaint themes, counting how often each comes up, and spotting patterns across all three episodes. Needs accurate grouping and counting, but it's routine analysis.

fable.why: Categorize 21 comments, count frequency per complaint, pick example quotes, spot cross-video patterns (intro length, music over voice, subtitles, host). Small dataset; Haiku high counts and groups accurately.
